sign: Missing, torn or cracked shingle sections.
alternativeExplanations: Damage extent and concealed decking condition remain unknown.
verification: Roofer examines covering and substrate; do not climb the roof.

sign: Lifted, curled or buckled shingle edges.
alternativeExplanations: Installation, weathering and movement can look similar.
verification: Roofer checks adhesion, layers and ventilation.

sign: Open, corroded or displaced flashing at penetrations or transitions.
alternativeExplanations: A visible joint is not necessarily a leaking joint.
verification: Roofer checks water-shedding overlaps and traces entry.

sign: Split or separated collar around a roof vent.
alternativeExplanations: Nearby damage may have a separate cause.
verification: Roofer verifies collar, adjacent flashing and deck.

sign: Damaged roof-valley water path.
alternativeExplanations: Surface debris alone does not prove concealed damage.
verification: Roofer checks drainage, covering and underlayment.

sign: Visible roof-plane depression or reported sagging.
alternativeExplanations: Perspective or framing movement; cause unverified.
verification: Structural assessment of framing and supports.

sign: Surface streaks without demonstrated covering failure.
alternativeExplanations: Staining alone does not establish a leak or replacement need.
verification: Ask roofer to distinguish surface growth from deterioration.

sign: Localized ceiling staining or peeling.
alternativeExplanations: Old repair, roof/plumbing leak or condensation.
verification: Check moisture, history and sources above; trace water path.

sign: Visible water entering or a report of an active leak.
alternativeExplanations: Entry location may differ from the source.
verification: Professional traces source; avoid wet electrical equipment.

sign: Sheathing moisture, frost, staining or corrosion.
alternativeExplanations: Rain entry and condensation can resemble each other.
verification: Assess weather timing, moisture, ventilation and air leakage.

sign: Ice accumulation at eaves with snow or reported water backup.
alternativeExplanations: Icicles alone do not prove water entered the house.
verification: Roofer assesses snowmelt, insulation and air leakage.

sign: Foundation cracks or displacement.
alternativeExplanations: Settlement, shrinkage and other movement need differentiation.
verification: Engineer documents width, displacement and progression.

sign: Reported uneven floors or racked/sticking openings.
alternativeExplanations: Humidity or installation can also affect fit.
verification: Engineer checks framing and foundation alignment.

sign: Visible damaged or cut framing.
alternativeExplanations: Strength cannot be determined from appearance alone.
verification: Structural professional assesses loads and repair scope.

sign: Basement/crawlspace dampness, deposits or water staining.
alternativeExplanations: Exterior runoff, groundwater, condensation or plumbing.
verification: Measure moisture and inspect drainage and plumbing paths.

sign: Ground slopes toward foundation or runoff reaches walls.
alternativeExplanations: Photo perspective cannot quantify grade.
verification: Measure elevations and trace runoff on site.

sign: Downspout discharges beside foundation.
alternativeExplanations: Discharge direction does not prove basement leakage.
verification: Verify outlet routing and ground drainage.

sign: Persistent ponding, erosion or runoff damage.
alternativeExplanations: Recent rain or irrigation may be temporary.
verification: Assess soil, elevations, utilities and lawful outlet.

sign: Dead limbs, trunk splits, decay or a new lean.
alternativeExplanations: Seasonal leaf loss alone does not show a dead tree.
verification: Arborist assesses tree and nearby targets.

sign: Reported or visible retaining-wall displacement.
alternativeExplanations: No photograph establishes wall stability.
verification: Engineer assesses wall, drainage and soil.

sign: Reported poor temperature control, noise or changed energy use.
alternativeExplanations: Controls, ducts, envelope and equipment can contribute.
verification: HVAC technician tests operation and load/airflow.

sign: Blocked filter, dirty coil or obstructed outdoor unit.
alternativeExplanations: Appearance alone cannot quantify performance loss.
verification: HVAC technician checks filter, coil and airflow.

sign: Ice on cooling coil or refrigerant tubing.
alternativeExplanations: Low airflow and refrigerant issues require different remedies.
verification: HVAC technician measures airflow and refrigerant condition.

sign: Water at air handler or condensate drain.
alternativeExplanations: Drain blockage, condensation or a separate leak.
verification: Trace drain and check condensate system.

sign: Disconnected, corroded or obstructed combustion vent.
alternativeExplanations: CO concentration and heat-exchanger integrity are not visible.
verification: Qualified combustion-safety assessment before use.

sign: Documented installation age or legible equipment label.
alternativeExplanations: Age is not a failure diagnosis or replacement deadline.
verification: Confirm model, service history and current operation.

sign: Scorching, melted insulation or reported hot outlet.
alternativeExplanations: Hidden wiring condition and load are unknown.
verification: Stop using affected equipment; electrician assesses.

sign: Exposed conductors or damaged electrical covers.
alternativeExplanations: Energization cannot be established visually.
verification: Avoid contact; electrician checks and repairs.

sign: Repeated breaker trips or reported flickering.
alternativeExplanations: Device fault, connection or load issue.
verification: Electrician traces fault; do not repeatedly reset.

sign: Dripping connection or reported active plumbing leak.
alternativeExplanations: Staining alone may reflect a historical leak.
verification: Plumber tests source and checks affected material.

sign: Reported slow drainage or backups.
alternativeExplanations: Local trap, branch drain, sewer or septic issue.
verification: Plumber localizes blockage; scope underground piping if indicated.

sign: Water or corrosion at water heater.
alternativeExplanations: Supply joint, relief valve or tank; replacement not automatic.
verification: Plumber identifies source before choosing repair.

sign: Swollen, stained or delaminated sink cabinet base.
alternativeExplanations: Past spill, condensation or plumbing leak.
verification: Check moisture and plumbing; assess concealed base only if warranted.

sign: Cracked wet-area finish or failed-looking joints.
alternativeExplanations: Surface cracks do not prove waterproofing failure.
verification: Assess moisture and waterproofing before finish replacement.

sign: Bathroom/kitchen exhaust visibly or reportedly terminates in attic.
alternativeExplanations: Fan sound alone does not establish outdoor exhaust.
verification: Verify duct termination and measured airflow.

sign: Floor cupping, swelling or lifting associated with moisture.
alternativeExplanations: Installation and substrate movement can also distort flooring.
verification: Measure moisture; identify source and substrate condition.

sign: Dated finish or style without functional damage.
alternativeExplanations: Preference is not deterioration.
verification: Separate optional remodeling from necessary repairs.

sign: Staining, peeling or deterioration around openings.
alternativeExplanations: Condensation and rain entry need different fixes.
verification: Assess flashing, seals and moisture source.

sign: Damaged siding or trim with possible moisture entry.
alternativeExplanations: Hidden wall condition remains unknown.
verification: Inspect drainage plane and flashing where warranted.

sign: Separated connection or deteriorated deck support.
alternativeExplanations: Fastener capacity cannot be established from overview images.
verification: Qualified structural assessment before loading suspect deck.

sign: Crushed exhaust duct, lint obstruction or reported long drying time.
alternativeExplanations: Clothes load or appliance faults can also extend drying.
verification: Qualified service checks exhaust path and operation.

sign: Report states an appliance failed an operating test.
alternativeExplanations: A listing photo does not establish appliance function.
verification: Service technician diagnoses before replacement.

sign: Shelter tubes or damaged wood with soil-lined galleries.
alternativeExplanations: Old damage does not establish active infestation.
verification: Pest specialist checks activity and damage extent.

sign: Reported suspect insulation or damaged material that may contain asbestos.
alternativeExplanations: Appearance cannot identify asbestos.
verification: Do not disturb; qualified professional evaluates sampling need.

sign: Peeling paint with documented pre-1978 context.
alternativeExplanations: Build year is a screening flag, not proof of lead.
verification: Certified professional checks before disturbing paint.

sign: Sewage backup or reported wet drainfield with odor.
alternativeExplanations: Ponding alone does not prove septic failure.
verification: Septic professional and local authority assess.

sign: Reported changed water color, odor or taste.
alternativeExplanations: Clear-looking water can still contain contaminants.
verification: Use appropriate laboratory water testing.

sign: Visible gap, separation or disconnected joint in a downspout.
alternativeExplanations: A disconnected joint can interrupt water routing; it does not establish interior damage or the final outlet location.
verification: Check continuity, connections and discharge routing from ground level or through a qualified contractor.

sign: Visible wall or wall-panel staining, tide marks or discolored patches.
alternativeExplanations: Prior wetting, condensation, surface contamination or other discoloration; a photo does not establish active moisture or mold.
verification: Verify material and location; assess moisture and history before identifying a cause.
